title: Sarbadars
capsule: The Sarbadars (Persian: سربداران, 'those who risk their heads') were a Shi'i-inclined political and religious movement that ruled a substantial portion of western Khurasan from Sabzavar following the disintegration of Ilkhanid authority after 1335. Founded around 1337 under Abd al-Razzaq, the movement combined popular Sufi orders with local gentry opposition to Mongol successor lords; internal tension between the secular amir faction and the radical dervish wing produced a succession of coups and assassinations among the rulers. At their greatest extent the Sarbadars controlled territory from Sabzavar to Nishapur. The movement ended when Khwaja Ali-yi Mu'ayyad peacefully submitted to Timur at Khurasan in 1381, and Timur absorbed the territory into his own empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Sarbadars' central Khurasanian territory is reasonably well attested through Persian chronicles, but the extent of their control over rural and mountain districts is uncertain.
